ultrasound_findings: 2 typical scenarios with VP diagnosis
Velamentous cord insertion (VCI) in lower uterine
segment (type 1)
– Cord inserts on membranes near internal os (IO)
Low-lying placenta with succenturiate lobe (SL) (type 2)
– Fetal vessels travel between placental lobes and cover
or are < 2 cm from IO
Transvaginal US (TVUS) + цветовой допpler are best tools
Use pulsed Doppler to prove vessels are fetal
Show arterial flow + document fetal heart rate
20-40% will resolve in 3rd trimester
↑ chance of resolution if VP diagnosed early (< 24
weeks)
↑ resolution if vessels are near IO but do not cover IO
Imaging recommendations
Identify placental cord insertion (PCI) carefully
– Should be routine part of anatomy scan
Look with TVUS and цветовой допpler if low-lying placenta
or cannot see PCI with transabdominal scan

Book p.836: Single Umbilical Artery

TERMINOLOGY: • Single umbilical artery (SUA) cord has 1 umbilical artery (UA)
and 1 umbilical vein (UV) instead of 2 UAs and 1 UV
IMAGING: • Free loop of cord with 2 vessels instead of 3

• Diagnosis can be made in any trimester
• SUA is isolated in 85% (no fetal anomalies)
○ Carries ↑ risk of fetal growth restriction (FGR)
○ ↑ incidence of abnormal placental morphology or
abnormal placental cord insertion
